body.statement:
For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), put
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4,
 \qquad
 M_{k,\ell}=M_A+M_B. \tag{24}
\]
The design-A and design-B structural enumerations used by \(\mathscr A\) have at most \(M_A\) and \(M_B\) templates, respectively. Every template has a semialgebraic Boolean description with at most
\[
 N_0=4\ell+10k+12,
 \qquad
 S_0=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1),
 \qquad
 D_0=4 \tag{25}
\]
variables, polynomial sign atoms, and polynomial degree.

Let
\[
 (A_S,D_S)=\mathsf{Samp}(N_0,S_0,D_0),
 \qquad
 (A_E,D_E)=\mathsf{Exist}(N_0,S_0+1,D_0) \tag{26}
\]
be coordinatewise nondecreasing published record-count and relative algebraic-degree bounds for bounded algebraic sampling and for existential realizability with a sample over the current coefficient field. Define
\[
 R_{k,\ell}=2+M_{k,\ell}(A_S+A_E),
 \qquad
 D_{k,\ell}=D_SD_E. \tag{27}
\]
Then \(R_{k,\ell}\) bounds the total number of algebraic sample and decision records generated by the one-sample/all-chart compiler, and hence its number of retained labeled outputs, while \(D_{k,\ell}\) bounds every final real-univariate algebraic degree after normalization back to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). If
\[
 Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1,
\]
there is a universal constant \(C\geq1\), independent of \(k\), \(\ell\), and the input, such that
\[
 R_{k,\ell}\leq 2^{CQ^C},
 \qquad
 D_{k,\ell}\leq 2^{CQ^C}. \tag{28}
\]

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles. Let \(\mathsf{Samp}_h\) and \(\mathsf{Exist}_h\) denote the corresponding published integer-height bounds, and let \(\mathsf{Flat}_h\) denote the explicit determinant, square-free-factorization, and root-isolation height bound for normalizing a finite real-algebraic tower to one real-univariate representation. For rational input coordinates whose numerators and denominators have binary length at most \(L\), set
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1),
 \qquad
 h_S=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_0,S_0,D_0,h_0), \tag{29}
\]
and let
\[
h_E=\mathsf{Exist}_h(N_0,S_0+1,D_0;h_0,h_S,D_S),
 \qquad
 h_F=\mathsf{Flat}_h(D_SD_E,h_S+h_E+1), \tag{30}
\]
where \(\mathsf{Exist}_h\) is evaluated after coefficients are represented in the degree-at-most-\(D_S\) real algebraic extension furnished by the initial sample. Define
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)=\max\{h_S,h_E,h_F\}.
\]
After flattening the extension tower and clearing only guarded denominators, every algebraic target or witness coordinate can be represented by a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(D_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating data of binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\). After enlarging the same universal constant if necessary,
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \leq
 \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}. \tag{31}
\]
Thus the record/output count and algebraic degree have the singly exponential fixed-alphabet bound (28), while the rational-height guarantee is the separate bound (31). A rational-input Turing implementation terminates. The decision enumerates structural charts, samples one point from their nonempty union, and applies an existential unequal-target test to each chart; connected-component description and target projection are not required decision stages, and no generic two-copy classifier is used.
body.justification: The theorem bounds the actual two-call engine and derives normalized degree by multiplying initial and relative extension degrees.
body.gap: Chart counts and residual-forest auxiliaries belong to optional diagnostics and must not multiply or enlarge the mandatory decision bound.
body.consumer: Exact implementations receive raw degree two for design A, raw degree three for design B, no chart multiplier, and a separately composed rational-height guarantee.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\).  We first count a direct polynomial presentation of each raw fiber.  In design A, the four endpoint vectors \(b_i\) contribute \(4\ell\) variables, and the two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells contribute \(8k\), giving
\[
N_A=4\ell+8k.                                                \tag{15}
\]
The endpoint nonnegativity and four normalizations use \(4\ell+4\) sign atoms.  Coefficient nonnegativity uses \(8k\), the four equations \(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\) use \(4k\), and the factorization equations use \(4k\ell\).  Therefore
\[
S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4.                                    \tag{16}
\]
Every factorization equation is bilinear in \((b,a)\), and all other design-A atoms are linear, so \(D_A=2\).

The raw design-B presentation adds the four margin coordinates, the \(k\) common-instrument coordinates, and the four response masses.  Hence
\[
N_B=N_A+4+k+4=4\ell+9k+8.                                  \tag{17}
\]
Margin positivity and normalization add five atoms, common-instrument positivity and normalization add \(k+1\), response-mass nonnegativity and normalization add five, and the response-level shared-\(Z\) equations add \(4k\).  Relevance can be written as the disjunction, over unordered pairs \(\{z,z'\}\), of the two strict signs of
\[
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z).                                    \tag{18}
\]
Allowing two sign atoms even for both orders gives the conservative addition \(2k(k-1)\).  Adding these quantities to (16) proves
\[
S_B\leq4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15.                           \tag{19}
\]
The shared-\(Z\) equations are quadratic because they contain \(m_ea_{ei}(z)\) and \(\pi_i g(z)\).  By the definition of \(q^X\), expression (18) is cubic after substitution, and no raw atom has larger degree.  Thus \(D_B=3\).  The target in (12) is linear, so its squared-distance inequality has degree two and does not enlarge either degree bound.

The effective semialgebraic sampling lemma, applied once to the raw design-\(d\) fiber over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), generates at most \(A_{S,d}\) records.  When the fiber is nonempty, let \(\xi\) be a primitive element for the sampled point \(x_0\).  The same lemma gives
\[
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\xi):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
\leq D_{S,d}.                                                \tag{20}
\]
The two coordinates of \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\) are linear sums of coordinates of \(x_0\), whence
\[
\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\subseteq\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\xi),
\qquad
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
\leq D_{S,d}.                                                \tag{21}
\]
There is then one existential-realizability call, over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\), on the raw fiber plus its one squared-distance atom.  It generates at most \(A_{E,d}\) records.  If it returns a witness with primitive element \(\upsilon\), then
\[
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\upsilon):
  \mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)]\leq D_{E,d}.                      \tag{22}
\]
Choose a spanning set of at most \(D_{S,d}\) elements for \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\) over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), and a spanning set of at most \(D_{E,d}\) elements for \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\upsilon)\) over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\).  Their pairwise products span the larger field over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), so (21)--(22) give
\[
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\upsilon):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
\leq D_{S,d}D_{E,d}=\mathcal D_d.                           \tag{23}
\]
Every returned coordinate \(u\) lies in this field.  In a vector space of dimension at most \(\mathcal D_d\), the \(\mathcal D_d+1\) elements \(1,u,\ldots,u^{\mathcal D_d}\) are linearly dependent over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Hence a nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(\mathcal D_d\) annihilates \(u\), and its minimal polynomial has no larger degree.  The cited tower-flattening, square-free-factorization, Thom-sign, and isolation procedures do not increase the field degree.  This proves the algebraic-degree bound by explicit multiplication of the two sequential relative degrees.  The two fixed status/output records together with the two algorithmic bounds give
\[
R_d=2+A_{S,d}+A_{E,d}.                                      \tag{24}
\]
There is no multiplication by a chart count because both calls use the single raw fiber.

For completeness, the diagnostic template count follows from the mixed-support structural theorem:
\[
M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
\qquad
M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4.                                     \tag{25}
\]
This finite list terminates if requested, but (25) does not occur in (23) or (24), and none of its residual, pivot, forest, or support variables occurs in (15) or (17).

Put \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\).  Equations (15)--(19) imply, after increasing a universal constant \(C\),
\[
N_d\leq CQ,
\qquad S_d\leq CQ,
\qquad D_d\leq3.                                           \tag{26}
\]
The published coordinatewise nondecreasing sampling and existential bounds in the effective semialgebraic lemma therefore give
\[
A_{S,d},D_{S,d},A_{E,d},D_{E,d}
\leq2^{CQ^C}.                                                \tag{27}
\]
Substitution into (23)--(24), followed by another enlargement of \(C\), proves
\[
R_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C},
\qquad
\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C}.                           \tag{28}
\]
For arbitrary real input, the only observable normalizations are divisions by \(r_e>0\), guaranteed by selected-table positivity.  Hence the raw coefficients lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The cited arithmetic, order, sign-determination, sampling, and real-root procedures terminate over the assumed effective oracle field.  Since there are only the two calls above, relative termination follows.

Suppose next that every rational input numerator and denominator has binary length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing the deleted simplex coordinates, forming each positive \(r_e\), dividing to obtain \(T_e\) and \(v_e\), and clearing those nonzero observable denominators in polynomials of degree at most three uses at most a quadratic number of elementary rational sums and products in \(Q\).  The conservative bound
\[
h_0=64Q^2(L+1)                                               \tag{29}
\]
therefore dominates the binary length of every cleared integer coefficient.  No latent pivot denominator is introduced by the raw presentation.

The integer-height part of the cited sampling result gives
\[
h_{S,d}=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_d,S_d,D_d,h_0).                    \tag{30}
\]
The second formula contains \(t_0\), represented in an extension of degree at most \(D_{S,d}\) and height at most \(h_{S,d}\).  Applying the relative existential height bound gives
\[
h_{E,d}=\mathsf{Exist}_h
(N_d,S_d+1,D_d;h_0,h_{S,d},D_{S,d}).                         \tag{31}
\]
Finally, multiplication matrices in dimension at most \(\mathcal D_d\), followed by square-free factorization and isolation, give
\[
h_{F,d}=\mathsf{Flat}_h
(\mathcal D_d,h_{S,d}+h_{E,d}+1).                            \tag{32}
\]
Equations (30)--(32) are sequential: the second-stage bound includes the first extension, and the flattening bound includes both heights and the product degree.  The height envelopes in the cited lemma, (26), and (27) imply, after one final enlargement of \(C\),
\[
H_{k,\ell}(L)
\leq\bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}.                     \tag{33}
\]
This is a separate rational-height guarantee; it is not identified with the singly exponential record and degree bounds in (28).  Square-free normalization and rational isolation give the stated exact representations.  All rational subroutines are finite, so the rational-input Turing implementation terminates.  The full-rigidity theorem proves that these two raw-fiber calls decide the causal target, while (25) remains solely an optional structural diagnostic.
